title: How a vaccine teaches your body

sources.title: How do vaccines work? (World Health Organization)

publish.title: How a vaccine teaches your body
publish.description: A short explanation of how vaccines train the immune system.

scenes.headline: How a vaccine teaches your body
scenes.narration: A vaccine is a rehearsal. Your body practises on part of a germ before the real thing.

scenes.headline: How it works
scenes.narration: A vaccine contains weakened or inactive parts of a germ. Your immune system responds, makes antibodies and memory cells, and responds faster next time.
items: A vaccine shows your body part of a germ
It makes antibodies and memory cells

scenes.headline: Memory is the point
scenes.narration: Memory cells stay alive after the germ is defeated. If you meet it again, the antibody response is much faster and more effective.

scenes.headline: Slower, but longer lasting
scenes.narration: The CDC notes that the immunity a vaccine builds takes longer to develop than borrowed antibodies, but it lasts longer.

scenes.headline: Ask a professional
scenes.narration: Ask your doctor or pharmacist which vaccines are right for you.
